title: Reconcile buffered input credits on intermittent streaming connections
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We observe intermittent streaming connections (mobile and flaky VPNs) where client-side reconnection semantics cause buffered input tokens to be committed late or not at all. This produces two classes of billing issues: (1) under-counted input credits when tokens are accepted but the commit path fails; (2) double-counting when resumed streams re-send the same tokens and the ingestor attributes both sets to the same session. This ticket designs and implements a defensive pipeline to ensure input/output token accounting is correct across disconnects, retries, and partial commits, without regressing streaming latency or increasing per-token cost.
acceptance_criteria: Metric: End-to-end token accounting reconciliation drift <= 0.1% for intermittent stream test harness under packet-loss up to 20%
No customer-visible duplicate input tokens billed after normal stream resume in 99.99% of synthetic replay tests
A reconciliation job runs within 10 minutes of a detected disconnect and adjusts billing ledger entries with audit logs for any retroactive credits/debits
New per-stream logging fields (resume_seq, commit_state, reserved_credits) are added to Trace and Console with retention for 30d
Integration tests introduced (unit + e2e harness) that cover: graceful resume, duplicate resend, delayed commit, mid-stream routing fallback
Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag 'stream-buffer-reconcile' and default-off for 48 hours in production canary before full enablement
tasks: Design data model for ephemeral reservation: reserved_credits + resume_seq + tentative_commit_id
Implement per-stream ephemeral buffer with sequence numbers in the front-line ingestor (runtime change)
Add idempotency markers to commit RPCs and ensure commit rpc returns committed_seq and applied_token_count
Create a reconciliation worker that compares ephemeral reservations against final commit ledger and emits adjustments
Instrument Console: add dashboard tile for stream-reconcile-errors, late-commit-rate, and retroactive-credit-amount
Add integration test harness that simulates network disconnects, replays, and concurrent resend semantics
Write migration to backfill reservations for last-48h using streaming event logs (best-effort)
updates: 2026-03-01: Created ticket after ops incident INC-2026-03-01-STREAM-METER where a set of mobile customers reported unexpected charges following flaky network conditions.
2026-03-03: Spike complete — ingest buffer approach with resume_seq looks feasible; prototype shows <3% latency P95 regression under normal load (notes linked).

2026-03-05: Design review with PM/Console/Infra — agreed on ephemeral reservation model and reconciliation worker. Concerns raised about the reconciliation job write amplification; decided to batch ledger updates per-minute.
2026-03-08: Implementation started for ingestor changes; added new fields to proto (resume_seq, tentative_commit_id).

2026-03-12: First end-to-end integration between ingestor and ledger service passes local tests. Identified race condition when fallback routing switches model mid-stream. Added task to gate fallback with reservation transfer handshake.
2026-03-14: Canary plan drafted; monitoring thresholds and alert runbooks created. Seeking approval to enable 'stream-buffer-reconcile' in Canary cluster (us-west-2) for subset of customers.
monitoring: New alerts: stream_reconcile_failure_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m, retroactive_credit_volume > $100/min. Dashboard panels: per-customer retroactive credits, late_commit_latency histogram.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Enable feature flag for 5% traffic in us-west-2 canary for 48h. Phase 2: 25% for 72h with tight monitoring. Phase 3: Global enable with 7-day review. If retroactive credits > $5000/day during canary, roll back and investigate.
notes: Trade-offs: We accept small delay in final commit visibility for some edge cases to avoid double-billing. Reconciliation cannot be perfectly realtime; design aims for eventual consistency with auditability. Consider follow-up to integrate with rate-limit quota delta API so retroactive credits flow into user quota refreshes.
